statement: A triangle $ABC$ with orthocenter $H$ is given. $P$ is a variable point on line $BC$. The perpendicular to $BC$ through $P$ meets $BH$, $CH$ at $X$, $Y$ respectively. The line through $H$ parallel to $BC$ meets $AP$ at $Q$. Lines $QX$ and $QY$ meet $BC$ at $U$, $V$ respectively. Find the shape of the locus of the incenters of the triangles $QUV$.
The numbers $a$, $b$, and $c$ are real. Prove that $(a^5+b^5+c^5+a^3c^2+b^3a^2+c^3b^2)^2\geq 4(a^2+b^2+c^2)(a^5b^3+b^5c^3+c^5a^3)$.

A class has 30 students. To celebrate 'Tu BiShvat' each student chose some dried fruits out of $n$ different kinds. Say two students are friends if they both chose from the same type of fruit. Find the minimal $n$ so that it is possible that each student has exactly 6 friends.

Let $n>1$ be an integer. Find all $r\in\mathbb{R}$ so that the system of equations in real variables $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$: $(rx_1-x_2)(rx_1-x_3)\cdots(rx_1-x_n)=(rx_2-x_1)(rx_2-x_3)\cdots(rx_2-x_n)=\cdots=(rx_n-x_1)(rx_n-x_2)\cdots(rx_n-x_{n-1})$ has a solution where $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ are pairwise distinct.

Define a ring in the plane as the set of points at distance at least $r$ and at most $R$ from a point $O$, where $r<R$ are positive reals. The area is $S$. An integer point has both coordinates integers. (a) For each positive integer $n$, show there exists a ring containing no integer point with $S>3n$ and $R<2^{2^n}$. (b) Show that each ring satisfying $100\cdot R < S^2$ contains an integer point.

In triangle $ABC$, the angle bisectors are $BE$ and $CF$ (where $E,F$ are on the sides), and their intersection is $I$. Point $N$ lies on the circumcircle of $AEF$, and $\angle IAN=90^\circ$. The circumcircle of $AEF$ meets line $NI$ a second time at $L$. Show that the circumcenter of $AIL$ lies on line $BC$.

Bilbo, Gandalf, and Nitzan play the following game. Nitzan picks a whole number between 1 and $2^{2022}$ inclusive and reveals it to Bilbo. Bilbo compiles a string of length 4044 from letters $a,b,c$. Nitzan looks at the string, chooses one of $a,b,c$, and removes all instances of that letter. The string (now from two letters) is revealed to Gandalf, who must guess Nitzan's number. Can Bilbo and Gandalf devise a strategy that always allows Gandalf to guess correctly, regardless of Nitzan's actions?

Let $f:\mathbb{Z}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function. It is known that for any integer $C$ the four functions $f(x,C)$, $f(C,x)$, $f(x,x+C)$, $f(x,C-x)$ are polynomials of degree at most 100. Prove that $f$ equals a polynomial in two variables and find its maximal possible degree.

Scalene triangle $ABC$ has incenter $I$ and circumcircle $\Omega$ with center $O$. $H$ is the orthocenter of triangle $BIC$, and $T$ is a point on $\Omega$ for which $\angle ATI=90^\circ$. Circle $(AIO)$ intersects line $IH$ again at $X$. Show that lines $AX$ and $HT$ intersect on $\Omega$.
